name: bare-path
usage:
```js
const path = require('bare-path')

path.join('foo', 'bar') // foo/bar on posix, foo\bar on windows
```

exports.name: path
exports.description: Path manipulation utilities, mirroring Node.js's `path` module.

members.name: path.basename
members.description: Returns the last portion of `path`, similar to the Unix `basename` command.

params.name: path
params.description: - The path to extract the last portion from.

params.name: suffix
params.description: - An optional suffix to remove from the end of the result, if it matches exactly.

returns.description: An empty string if `suffix` equals `path` exactly.

throws.condition: thrown if `path`, or a defined `suffix`, is not a string.

members.name: path.delimiter
members.description: The platform-specific path delimiter: `;` on Windows, `:` elsewhere.

members.name: path.dirname
members.description: Returns the directory name of `path`, similar to the Unix `dirname` command.

params.name: path
params.description: - The path to extract the directory name from.

throws.condition: thrown if `path` is not a string.

members.name: path.extname
members.description: Returns the extension of `path`, from the last `.` to the end of the string.

params.name: path
params.description: - The path to extract the extension from.

returns.description: An empty string if `path` has no `.` in its last segment, or if that segment's only `.` is its first character (for example a dotfile).

throws.condition: thrown if `path` is not a string.

members.name: path.isAbsolute
members.description: Returns `true` if `path` is an absolute path.

returns.description: On Windows, a drive-qualified path such as `C:\foo` is also absolute; on POSIX, only paths starting with `/` are absolute.

throws.condition: thrown if `path` is not a string.

members.name: path.join
members.description: Joins all given path segments using the platform-specific separator, then normalizes the result.

params.name: paths
params.description: - The path segments to join together, in the order given.

throws.condition: thrown if any path segment is not a string.
thrown if `path` is not a string.

members.name: path.posix
members.description: The POSIX-specific implementation of the `path` methods.

members.name: path.relative
members.description: Returns the relative path from `from` to `to`.

params.name: from
params.description: - The path to resolve the relative path from.

params.name: to
params.description: - The path to resolve the relative path to.

returns.description: Both `from` and `to` are resolved to absolute paths before comparing, and an empty string is returned if they resolve to the same path.

throws.condition: thrown if `from` or `to` is not a string.

members.name: path.resolve
members.description: Resolves a sequence of paths or path segments into an absolute path.

params.name: args
params.description: - The path segments to resolve, processed from right to left until an absolute path is constructed.

returns.description: Falls back to the current working directory (or that of the resolved drive, on Windows) if none of the given segments is absolute.

throws.condition: thrown if any path segment is not a string.

members.name: path.sep
members.description: The platform-specific path segment separator: `\` on Windows, `/` elsewhere.

members.name: path.toNamespacedPath
members.description: Converts `path` to a namespace-prefixed path on Windows; returns `path` unchanged on POSIX.

returns.description: On Windows, resolves `path` and prefixes UNC paths with `\\?\UNC\` and drive-letter paths with `\\?\`; other paths (including non-string input) are returned unchanged.

members.name: path.win32
members.description: The Windows-specific implementation of the `path` methods.
